title: Structures, members and member access
learningObjectives: Explain the C concept and its rules.
Trace the example and describe data flow.
Identify relevant failure and boundary cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A structure type groups named members, which may have different types, into one object. The dot operator accesses a member through a structure object. Each member has its own declared type and value.
understand.whyItMatters: Structures model records such as products, coordinates and users while keeping related fields together under one object name.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
A structure type groups named members, which may have different types, into one object. The dot operator accesses a member through a structure object. Each member has its own declared type and value.

Check all return values, object lifetimes, types and preconditions. Enable compiler warnings and test expected as well as failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: item is one structure object with an int code and double price. The dot operator selects each member for reading.

practise.guidedTask: Draw the structure object and label each member with its type.
practise.independentTask: Define a structure for a repair ticket with an identifier, status and estimated cost. Initialize and print it.
hints: A structure's members appear in declaration order, but padding may exist between them.
Structure assignment copies the structure value, including its members.
Do not assume a structure's byte layout is identical across compilers or platforms.
